title: Record S15's review round 1
message:
Record S15's review round 1

The four findings on MR !22 (one P2, three P3), what each fix changed,
the ablation of the fixes and their verification: the unit suite, a live
job with a database that refuses both a write and its undo, the gates
that run the changed commands, and the local CI matrix.

title: Describe the purchases that stand in the vessel system document
message:
Describe the purchases that stand in the vessel system document

The checked purchases passage now says what review round 1 of MR !22
changed: a database that does not answer refuses a purchase before the
gold is taken; a purchase, a summons or a spawn whose undo cannot be
written stands and stays paid; a trade-in whose undo cannot be recorded
keeps the charge for the staff to settle; a refused summons is written
back hull first; and a summoned hull's vehicles are put off where she
lay.

title: Keep a spawned hull whose rows cannot be removed
message:
Keep a spawned hull whose rows cannot be removed

A spawn whose rows cannot be written rolled itself back without looking
at whether the rollback's delete committed, and shipbuy then returned
the price. With the reply to her runtime row lost (the last write, and
made) and the database out of reach for the delete, the rows held her
whole record with no hull in memory to write over them: the next boot
rebuilt her for a buyer who had the price back.

The rollback now deletes her rows before it takes her out of play, as
shippurge does. When the delete does not commit she stays in play and
the spawn returns her slot, so a purchase stands and stays paid, and her
next save writes her rows. Every outcome is a paid hull, or after a
crash a paid buyer without one, never a free hull.

Review of MR !22, finding 3.

title: Let a purchase stand when it cannot be written back
message:
Let a purchase stand when it cannot be written back

A hull write that fails is undone by writing the hull back, and the
price was then returned whether or not that write-back succeeded. The
two failures are usually one event: a reply lost on a statement the
server ran is the start of an outage, and the write-back cannot
reconnect. The rows then keep the purchase and the player file has the
gold back. Nothing saves the fleet periodically (save_all_vessels() runs
at copyover and at shutdown), so the rows keep it until her next
shipyard job: a crash before then boots her with a gunner, a weapon, a
refit, a name or a summons nobody paid for.

The gold is returned, and "nothing was done" said, only when the
write-back succeeded:

- vessel_purchase_recorded() (the seven shipyard jobs) puts the bought
  hull back in memory, writes her once more and keeps the price, as
  vessel_sale_recorded() lets a sale stand.
- shipsummon carries on as summoned. When she makes port her manifest is
  saved with her runtime row, so rows that missed the emptied hold
  cannot bring cargo in with her.
- The trade-in has rebuilt the old hull by then: it keeps the charge and
  tells the captain and the staff, who settle it.
  vessel_trade_in_undo() reports whether she is as she was in play and
  in her rows.
- vessel_charge() refuses the purchase before any gold is taken when the
  database does not answer, so one that is away before the command
  charges nothing and does nothing, as before.

Tests: a hire and a summons whose reply is lost with the database out of
reach for the write-back (vessel_test_database_away()), and a purchase
refused before the charge by a database that does not answer.

Review of MR !22, finding 2.

title: Write a refused summons back hull first
message:
Write a refused summons back hull first

The summons writes the emptied manifest before the stowed hull, so a
crash between the two cannot bring her in with the cargo it leaves
behind. Its write-back ran the same two writes in the same order with
the old state: the full manifest, then the hull as she was. When the
reply to her stowed runtime row was lost, a stop between those two left
rows that said stowed, due at the shipyard, hold full.

The hull is written back before the manifest. A stop between the two
leaves her where she was with an empty manifest, the loss the forward
order already accepts.

Review of MR !22, finding 4.

title: Put a summoned hull's carts off where she lay
message:
Put a summoned hull's carts off where she lay

shipsummon saves the summons before anything alongside or aboard is
touched, so by the time her vehicles are released the hull's own
position is already the summoning shipyard's.
vehicle_release_all_from_vessel() copies that position into each
vehicle: a cart was left in the room where she lay with the coordinates
of the shipyard, in memory and in its vehicle_data row. A vehicle's
coordinates are where it drives from and where boot places it, so one
"drive" carried the cart and its riders to the shipyard, however long
the hull's passage, and after a boot the cart stood there.

The vehicles are now released from the copy of the hull taken before
the summons, which still holds where she was. The summons test carries
a cart and checks its room, its coordinates and its row.

Review of MR !22, finding 1.

title: Leave a refused summons and a failed trade-in as they were
message:
Leave a refused summons and a failed trade-in as they were

Found by a read of the build before hand-off.

A refused summons had already cast off the hull alongside, released her
vehicles and stopped her autopilot. It now saves her as cast off and
stopped (the autopilot's state is remembered beside the copy of the
hull) and touches the world only once that is saved. The emptied
manifest is written before the stowed hull, so a crash between the two
does not bring her in with her cargo.

A trade-in whose rebuild fails takes the same undo as one that cannot be
recorded, and the undo does not write a hull whose rooms could not be
recreated. A spawn writes the runtime row last: rows left by a rollback
whose purge failed hold the slot at boot instead of becoming a hull.

vessel_save_one() attempts every part again; only vessel_save_hull()
stops at the first that fails. A sale that stands writes the hull once
more. A delivery that can neither be recorded nor taken back tells the
captain and the staff that the books may be wrong.

The tests compare hulls through one helper (clang-tidy refused the
struct memcmp), and cover the summons under autopilot with a hull
alongside, the delivery's lost manifest and its unknown outcome, the
fleet save after a failed owner write, and a mob's charge.

title: Play the refused purchase as the loss session's own captain
message:
Play the refused purchase as the loss session's own captain

The staff character owns harbor fixtures at both docks, so his trade-in
took one of them instead of the check's raft. The refused hull and
trade-in now run inside the two-character loss session: the harness
lists a design and has the database refuse its runtime row before the
session, and Vesselmate, who owns only the check's boat, orders both on
the dock. The helper takes the design's id as a second argument.

title: Play a purchase and a trade-in the database refuses in the loss gate
message:
Play a purchase and a trade-in the database refuses in the loss gate

No unit world generates ship interiors, so shipbuy's and the trade-in's
refused hull write are played in game: the harness adds a CHECK
constraint that refuses one design's runtime row, Kohdee buys that
design and trades his raft in for it, and the gate checks both messages,
his player file's gold, the hull's rows, and the same trade-in once the
constraint is dropped.

title: Save the gold and write the ship's side in each vessel purchase and payout
message:
Save the gold and write the ship's side in each vessel purchase and payout

The vessel commands S11 did not reach wrote the ship's side to MariaDB at
once and moved the gold in memory only. Each now writes and checks both
stores inside the command (work item #14).

A purchase takes the gold first: vessel_charge() saves the debit and
refuses the purchase when the player file cannot be written. If the
ship's side then cannot be written, the hull goes back to the copy taken
before the work, is written back, and the gold is returned. A payout
writes the ship's side first and puts the item back when the gold cannot
be saved; a put-back that cannot be written lets the sale stand.

shiphire, shipweapon and shipequip (buying and selling), shiprearm,
dock shiprepair, shipupgrade and shipchristen go through
vessel_purchase_recorded() and vessel_sale_recorded(), which write the
hull with vessel_save_hull(). shipbuy refunds a failed spawn; a trade-in
whose hull or payment cannot be recorded is rebuilt back; a summons is
saved before the hull leaves the world; the bounty pay-off and marque
read the row back when their write reports a failure; contractdeliver
writes the contract and the manifest in one transaction, then pays.

shipupgrade now saves the runtime row with the refit bit: the raised
ceilings were in memory only until the next runtime save.
